utterance:
Samuel, putting it all together - the pain starting around the belly button and moving to the lower right, the sickness, loss of appetite, the fever, and what I found when I examined you - this looks very much like appendicitis, an inflamed appendix. It is not a stomach bug. This needs to be assessed by the surgeons at the hospital today, and most likely treated with an operation to remove the appendix. It's a common operation and people your age do very well, but it's important not to delay, because an inflamed appendix can burst if left. 

Here's the plan: I'm sending you straight to the emergency department now, and I'll phone ahead so they're expecting you. Please don't eat or drink anything from now on, in case you need an operation today. Is there someone who can drive you to the hospital right now? You shouldn't drive yourself with this pain.
reply: Can't I just go home and wait for it to pass?

utterance: I understand it's not what you were hoping to hear, but no - this is not safe to wait out at home. An inflamed appendix does not settle on its own; it gets worse, and if it bursts you can become very sick with infection throughout the belly, which means a bigger operation and a longer time in hospital. Caught early, like now, it's usually a short keyhole operation and you're home within a day or two. You've already got all the classic signs, so the hospital is the right place. Who can take you there now - a family member, housemate or your boss? If no one is available I'll arrange an ambulance.
reply: Okay, my mum can drive me.

awards.label: Refer to the emergency department today for surgical assessment
Phone the emergency department with a handover

utterance: Good. Call your mum now and go straight to the emergency department - don't go home first. I've sent a letter with them and I'm phoning the hospital so they know you're coming with suspected appendicitis. Please remember: nothing to eat or drink, not even water, until the hospital team says it's okay. If while you're on the way the pain suddenly becomes much worse or spreads across your whole belly, you feel faint, or you can't stop vomiting, tell the hospital staff immediately as soon as you arrive, or call 000 if you're held up. Take any pain relief they offer there rather than more paracetamol now. Do you have any questions before you go?
reply: Nah, I just want to get it over with.
